title: Number of Social Visit Pass Holders from China who Have Been Arrested
what_it_is: Number of Social Visit Pass Holders from China who Have Been Arrested

sections.label: Chinese visitor arrests percentage
sections.summary: No increase in number or percentage of short-term visitors from China arrested since February's mutual visa exemption, and the percentage would be lower than last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To answer Mr Leong's question directly, there has been no increase in the number or percentage of short-term visitors from China arrested in Singapore since the mutual visa exemption arrangements were implemented in February this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Even if we take into account the 14 Chinese nationals I referred to earlier, the percentage of Chinese visitors arrested in Singapore would be lower than the corresponding percentage last year.

sections.label: Tourism sector contribution
sections.summary: The tourism sector contributed $27.2 billion in tourism receipts in 2023 and employed more than 71,000 workers as of December 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Just as an example, the tourism sector contributed $27.2 billion in tourism receipts in 2023 and employed more than 71,000 workers as of December 2023.

sections.label: Mutual visa exemption assessment
sections.summary: The mutual visa exemption with China was a carefully assessed decision that security, criminal and immigration risks were manageable and economic and bilateral benefits significant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The mutual visa exemption with China was a carefully assessed and weighed decision, that the security, criminal and immigration risks were manageable, that the economic and bilateral benefits would be significant and that, overall, it is in Singapore's interests to have this arrangement with China.

sections.label: PSP stance on foreigners
sections.summary: He thanks him for confirming the PSP's stance to keep Singapore open to foreigners and visitors, which is critical to Singapore's economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: First and foremost, I thank him for confirming the PSP's stance to keep Singapore open to foreigners and to visitors, because that is critical to Singapore's economy and to continue to have Singapore be a vibrant place for residents and visitors alike.

sections.label: Reviewing laws for evolving crimes
sections.summary: Laws have been revised and measures taken on online scams, and laws must be monitored and reviewed for evolving transnational crimes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Over the years, we have been revising our Criminal Procedure Code and Penal Code to enhance our measures to take into account all these offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Mr Leong would also be familiar with the whole slew of measures that we have undertaken recently and also moving forward when it comes to online scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, I take Mr Leong's point that with increasing number of visitors and not only that, with the increasing use of technology to commit transnational crimes, that we must always monitor and review our laws to make sure that they take into account the evolving nature of crimes.
